title: FixedOrderFactor-lean: a Lean 4 formalization of the order-r correction factor for mean squares of L(1, chi)
description:
Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying the paper “The factor 35/34: fourth powers in the mean square of L(1, χ) over quartic characters” (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23488965). Restricted to characters of order r, with the Euler factors at a finite set N of primes removed, the random Euler product model for the mean square of L(1, χ) exceeds the full-family value by R_r(N) = ζ^(N)(r)²/ζ^(N)(2r). For r = 4 and N = {2} this factor is 35/34.

The development proves:

  • the order-r local factor;
  • the Euler product and the sum over coprime pairs for R_r(N);
  • the surviving pairs (m, n) = (d aʳ, d bʳ);
  • the model mean and its limit;
  • the shape of R_r(N): it exceeds 1, decreases in r, and tends to 1;
  • the Bernoulli closed form for even r;
  • the quartic constants 35/34, 7π²/68 and 7/136 = (1/20)(35/34);
  • orthogonality for the characters with χʳ = 1 modulo a prime;
  • the finite part of the Chebyshev bias in families p ≡ a (mod M) of fixed order: the orbit-average sums, the prime-square term as s times the square-root count β(M, a, s), the class criterion, and the vanishing of β in the imaginary families unless 8 ∣ r.

The statements are in Challenge.lean. Lean's comparator checks them against the proofs, with the definition bodies compared, and the proofs are replayed in the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels. No sorry, no native_decide; standard axioms only. The changes in each version are described in the release notes on GitHub: github.com/jkfarland-bot/FixedOrderFactor-lean/releases.
notes: AI assistance: the Lean code in this record was drafted and repaired by Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, from the statements and proofs of the companion paper "The factor 35/34: fourth powers in the mean square of L(1, χ) over quartic characters" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23488965), and compiled locally with lake. Every proof is checked by the Lean kernel, and Comparator replays the solution against the statement file under the Lean, NanoDa and con-ron kernels. The author, Joseph S. Farland, chose the scope, directed the work, and is responsible for the contents. No external human reviewer has checked the formalization.
